guidance.sentence: Assuming the continuation of current market conditions as well as constant exchange rates, for the fourth quarter of 2026, Amphenol expects sales to be in the range of $10.3 to $10.5 billion, representing an approximately 60% increase over the prior year quarter.
Adjusted Diluted EPS is expected to be in the range of $0.81 to $0.83, representing a 65% to 69% increase from the fourth quarter of 2025.

For the full year 2026, Amphenol expects sales to be in the range of $36.9 billion to $37.1 billion, representing an approximately 60% increase over prior year, while Adjusted Diluted EPS is expected to be in the range of $2.82 to $2.84, representing an approximately 70% increase over prior year.

For the full year 2026, Amphenol expects sales to be in the range of $36.9 billion to $37.1 billion, representing an approximately 60% increase over prior year, while Adjusted Diluted EPS is expected to be in the range of $2.82 to $2.84, representing an approximately 70% increase over prior year.

In addition, given the continued better-than-expected performance of the CommScope business, Amphenol now expects the business to generate full-year sales of $5.1 billion and to be $0.18 accretive to the Company’s Adjusted Diluted EPS in 2026 which is reflected in our outlook.

In addition, given the continued better-than-expected performance of the CommScope business, Amphenol now expects the business to generate full-year sales of $5.1 billion and to be $0.18 accretive to the Company’s Adjusted Diluted EPS in 2026 which is reflected in our outlook.
The Company estimates acquisition-related costs in the fourth quarter of 2026 of approximately $0.01 per share primarily related to external transaction costs.

writeup.headline: Amphenol rates Hold: very strong AI-driven growth offset by absolute valuation that is high and moderate leverage.
writeup.thesis: Amphenol scores 62, a Hold, 3 points short of the Buy band. Growth is the standout factor (83), with TTM revenue growth of 54.2% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 55.0% year on year, though growth slowed by 3.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is solid at 69 on a 27.0% operating margin and 16.2% FCF margin, and news is supportive (71) after a Q3 beat and Q4 guidance of $10.3 to $10.5 billion in sales. Holding the score back are valuation (34), with P/FCF of 42.4x and EV/EBIT of 27.2x high in absolute terms and an FCF yield 2.6 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and a middling balance sheet (48) with net debt at 2.84x FCF. Against its own history, valuation is near the middle of its own history, with P/S more expensive than at 44 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: IT datacom is 48% of sales and largely AI-driven, a concentration management itself flagged
Growth slowed by 3.4 pp from the previous quarter; a further slowdown would hit the strongest factor
Absolute valuation is high, with an FCF yield 2.6 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield
Acquisition activity (CommScope plus about $1.6B of new deals) adds integration risk and keeps leverage elevated, with cash covering only 0.29 of debt
Diluted share count up 1.3% year on year
what_would_change: A 3-point gain in the composite would reach Buy, for example from a better valuation score after a share price pullback or continued earnings growth
Paying down debt to lift the balance sheet score from 48 could also add the needed points
A drop of 18 points to below 45 would be needed for Sell, likely requiring a sharp growth slowdown alongside weaker guidance or trend
A break in price trend (currently 0.4% below its 50-day average) or negative news on AI demand would push the score lower
